metadata.title: MC-001: Restriction Enzyme Digestion with NEB Standard Digest
metadata.purpose: Perform a 50 uL analytical or preparative restriction digest using a selected NEB restriction enzyme and matching NEBuffer.
metadata.scope: Training/library SOP draft. Select enzyme-specific buffer, temperature, units, methylation sensitivity, star-activity risk, and heat-inactivation condition from NEB guidance before bench use.
beforeYouBegin: Use NEBcloner or the enzyme product page to confirm buffer, incubation temperature, methylation sensitivity, star-activity risk, and heat-inactivation option.
Use high-quality DNA free of ethanol, phenol, salts, SDS, or guanidinium carryover.
For double digests, confirm both enzymes have compatible buffer and temperature conditions.
Keep restriction enzymes on ice or a cold block and add them last.

materials.name: Purified DNA substrate
materials.specification: Plasmid, PCR product, or genomic DNA compatible with the selected restriction enzyme

materials.name: Selected NEB restriction enzyme
materials.storage: Keep on ice or a cold block during setup; return to -20 deg C promptly and minimize freeze-thaw cycles

materials.name: Matching NEBuffer
materials.specification: Use buffer selected for the enzyme or compatible double digest

materials.name: Required enzyme-specific additive
materials.specification: Such as rAlbumin, ATP, DTT, or activator; use only if specified

materials.name: DNA cleanup column or gel extraction kit

equipment.name: Ice bucket or cold block
equipment.settings: Keep reaction tubes and enzymes cold during setup

steps.action: Label reaction tubes and keep them on ice during setup.
For a typical reaction, combine DNA, 10X NEBuffer, nuclease-free water to near-final volume, and any required additive.
Add restriction enzyme last and follow enzyme-specific unit recommendations.

materialUses.rawText: A common starting point is about 1 uL enzyme for 1 ug DNA

parameters.rawText: about 1 uL enzyme for 1 ug DNA

steps.criticalNotes: The source calls this a common starting point; follow enzyme-specific unit recommendations.

steps.action: Mix gently by pipetting and briefly collect liquid by microcentrifugation.
Incubate at the enzyme-specific temperature and time; for cloning-scale digests, use the manufacturer-recommended condition for complete digestion.
If the digest will be analyzed directly, add appropriate loading dye or stop solution and load an aliquot on an agarose gel.
If digested DNA will be ligated or assembled, remove enzyme by heat inactivation if allowed, column cleanup, gel extraction, or phenol/chloroform cleanup.
For vector preparation, gel-purify the correctly cut backbone when undigested vector or wrong-size products could create background.
Confirm expected band sizes from a plasmid map or in silico digest, quantify purified vector and insert for cloning, and record the run.

acceptanceCriteria.description: Confirm from a plasmid map or in silico digest.
If no cut is observed, check methylation sensitivity, buffer choice, enzyme activity, DNA purity, and site presence.

steps.expectedResult: Digest result and validation record are available.

controls.name: Undigested DNA control
controls.description: Run on an agarose gel when interpretation matters.

expectedOutputs: Restriction-digested DNA with expected band sizes.
Quantified purified vector and insert after digestion/cleanup for cloning where applicable.

troubleshooting.cause: Wrong buffer, methylated site, too little enzyme, or poor DNA purity.
troubleshooting.solution: Check the enzyme page, use fresh buffer, clean DNA, and extend incubation within NEB guidance.

troubleshooting.cause: Too much enzyme, wrong buffer, high glycerol, or long incubation.
troubleshooting.solution: Keep enzyme volume low, use recommended buffer, and avoid overdigestion.

troubleshooting.cause: Partial digest, plasmid conformation, or wrong construct map.
troubleshooting.solution: Compare to an undigested control and verify sequence/map.
Clean up digested DNA and confirm compatible phosphorylated ends.

safety: Wear a lab coat, gloves, and eye protection.
Keep enzymes cold as specified; minimize freeze-thaw cycles and return enzymes to -20 deg C promptly.
Handle UV transilluminators and DNA stains according to local EHS guidance.
